name: Garlic-Butter Salmon & Crispy Potatoes
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Put the potatoes on a sheet pan. Toss with 4 tsp olive oil, 1 tsp seasoned salt, and the black pepper. Roast cut-side down for 15 minutes.
Push the potatoes to one side. Add the green beans and toss them with the remaining 2 tsp olive oil and a pinch of seasoned salt.
Pat the salmon dry. Mix melted butter, garlic, garlic powder, smoked paprika, and the remaining seasoned salt. Spoon it over the salmon.
Place salmon on the pan and bake everything 10–12 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily and reaches 125–130°F for moist salmon or 145°F for fully cooked.
Squeeze lemon over the salmon and green beans. Plate it hot.
note: The butter-garlic topping tastes rich; the lemon keeps it from feeling heavy.
leftovers: Serves two for dinner, with two portions ready for lunch or another dinner.
prep: Protein — 4 salmon fillets, 5–6 oz each.
Sauce / finish — 2 tbsp butter, melted.

prep: Bowl 1 — Chicken: Cut 1 1/2 lb chicken tenderloins into chunks. Add 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp seasoned salt, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp onion powder, and 1/2 tsp black pepper.

steps: Heat the oven and bake the refrigerated biscuits according to the package directions. Keep them warm while you make the chicken and gravy.
Cut 1 1/2 lb chicken tenderloins into bite-size chunks. Toss with 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp seasoned salt, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp onion powder, and 1/2 tsp black pepper.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high. Add the seasoned chicken in one layer and cook 6–8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned and 165°F in the center. Transfer the chicken to a plate.
Reduce heat to medium. Melt 2 tbsp butter in the same skillet. Sprinkle in 2 tbsp flour and whisk continuously for 1 minute.
Slowly pour in 2 cups chicken broth while whisking, then whisk in 1/2 cup milk. Simmer 3–5 minutes until the gravy coats the back of a spoon.
Return the chicken to the gravy. If using the optional 1 cup corn, stir it in now and simmer 2 minutes until hot. Taste before adding extra salt.
Split the warm biscuits into serving bowls. Spoon the chicken and gravy over the biscuits and serve immediately.
note: Chicken-and-biscuits comfort without a two-hour Sunday project.
